Options for groundplotqc

Source: R/options.R
groundplotqc_options.Rd

groundplotqc functions read their settings from function arguments, the rule set and R options. This page lists the R options.

Option names

Each option is named groundplotqc.<setting>, with the setting's name in lower snake case after the dot.

Where a setting's value comes from

A function takes each setting from the first of these that gives a value:

  1. the function's argument;

  2. the rule set;

  3. the option, set with options();

  4. the built-in default.

Options

  • groundplotqc.lang: the language of report text, a code of two or three lower-case letters such as "fr". Built-in: "en". A text with no row in the language is shown in English. In a language other than English, pre-flight's text_id_fallback lists each registered rule's message that has no row in it.

  • groundplotqc.severity: severities by rule ID, a named character vector such as c(some_rule = "warning"), each rule named once. Built-in: none, so each rule keeps its registered severity. In a rule set the rules rows' severity column gives this tier. Pre-flight checks each entry (rule_id_unknown, rule_set_override_invalid); a pre-flight check's own outcome can't be changed.

  • groundplotqc.example_cap: how many distinct failing values a results row shows in its examples column. Built-in: 5. It also caps how many values design_geometry_inconsistent and design_duplicate_signature list in an issue's expected, which then ends with a count of the rest; at 0, expected is NA, as examples is.

  • groundplotqc.column_level_min_n: the fewest records a column must have in a group before a rule that fails on all of them is recorded as one column-level issue. Built-in: 10.

  • groundplotqc.raw_na_policy: when a raw NA is an error (raw_na) in a column outside the primary and foreign keys, whose missing values pk_missing and fk_unassigned report (Layer 4, see gpq_check_conformance()): "when_sentinels", only in a column whose type has missing-value codes; "always"; or "never". Built-in: "when_sentinels".

  • groundplotqc.rogue_codes: values that stand in for a missing value but aren't the agreed codes (sentinel_rogue_code), compared as numbers in a column stored as numbers, as text otherwise. A value is never one when it is a code of the column's code list, a missing-value code of the column's type, an unknown code of the attribute, or another type's missing-value code that sentinel_wrong_type reports. Built-in: c("-999", "UNK", "NA", "N/A").

  • groundplotqc.unknown_codes: codes for "unknown" by attribute, such as c(species = "UNKN.SPP") (species_unknown_code); an attribute may be named more than once. Built-in: none.

  • groundplotqc.coordinate_attributes: attribute names, in any table, that coordinate_out_of_bounds checks against the dictionary's minimum and maximum, and that value_below_min and value_above_max then leave alone. Built-in: none.

  • groundplotqc.code_set_max_values: the most distinct values a text column without a code list can hold and still be reported by undeclared_code_set, which judges only a column holding more values than this, not counting NA, blanks, missing-value codes and unknown codes. Built-in: 25.

  • groundplotqc.code_set_skip_attributes: attributes undeclared_code_set never judges. Built-in: none.

  • groundplotqc.code_set_skip_pattern: one regular expression; undeclared_code_set doesn't judge an attribute whose name matches it. Built-in: none.

  • groundplotqc.design_geometry_table, groundplotqc.design_geometry_by and groundplotqc.design_geometry_columns: the table design_geometry_inconsistent reads, the attributes that group its records, and the attributes that must agree within a group. Built-in: none.

  • groundplotqc.subplot_label_table and groundplotqc.subplot_label_columns: the table subplot_label_ambiguous reads and the attributes that label its records. Built-in: none.

  • groundplotqc.design_signature_table, groundplotqc.design_signature_by and groundplotqc.design_signature_columns: the table design_duplicate_signature reads, its foreign key to the records compared, and the attributes whose values, over the table's rows that name a record, make up that record's signature. Built-in: none.

  • groundplotqc.fallback_class: by rule ID, the class an issue takes when its rule's class is depends and nothing else settles it, such as c(some_rule = "source"): each class "source" or "harmonization", each rule named once. Built-in: none, so such an issue is unclassified. Unlike the severity setting, the first tier that gives it gives all of it: an argument or a rule set naming one rule replaces every entry of the option, so the other rules have none. In a rule set's settings rows it is written as "rule_id=class" parts, and in every tier a rule ID can't be empty, begin or end with a space, tab or line break, or hold ";" or "=". Pre-flight stops on a rule ID that isn't registered (rule_id_unknown).

In a rule set's settings rows, a whole number has type integer, a setting with several values gives them joined by "; ", and a named one gives "name=value" parts. In every tier, a code can't be empty, begin or end with a space, tab or line break, or hold ";". In groundplotqc.unknown_codes the same holds for each name, and neither a code nor a name can hold "=". The same holds for each table and attribute name in groundplotqc.coordinate_attributes, groundplotqc.code_set_skip_attributes and the eight options above.

Options apply to every specification checked in the session. A table or attribute an option names that a specification doesn't have is reported by pre-flight as a warning (option_unknown_name) and otherwise ignored; given as an argument or in a rule set, such a name stops pre-flight (setting_unknown_name). In groundplotqc.design_geometry_by, groundplotqc.subplot_label_columns and groundplotqc.design_signature_columns, one such name drops the whole option, so its check doesn't run.

More options are added by the versions that bring the settings they control.
